media.alt: AKU seminar on World No Tobacco Day

content.text: "Tobacco is the world's single largest preventable cause of death," said Professor Javaid Ahmed Khan, Head, Section of Pulmonary and Critical Medicine of Aga Khan University, during his talk on "The Tobacco Epidemic in Pakistan." He highlighted the government's misperception regarding the government's "need and reliance on revenues generated from this industry" and urged the medical community to "make our government realise that tobacco control is highly cost-effective as a basic public health package". Professor Javaid called for urgent official measures to substitute tobacco with alternative crops and support farmers for a specific time period, and further reasoned that governments of the developed countries must take responsibility to pressure transnational companies in preventing them from targeting children and youth in the developing world. Alarming figures were revealed in this context regarding 2002 budgets for tobacco-related education by the Ministry of Health - Rs 2 million as against Rs 61 million for advertising by a tobacco company.

Assistant Professor Dr Suleman Haque, from the Pulmonology section, clarified several common misperceptions on the myths and realities of nicotine withdrawal symptoms. Professor Riaz Qureshi of the Department of Family Medicine, AKU, spoke of the increasingly important role of the family physician in tobacco control measures, while Assistant Professor in the department, Dr Marie Andrades, highlighted important aspects on how to motivate patients to quit smoking. Professor Ehsanullah Syed of the Department of Psychiatry voiced his views on the reasons for the use of tobacco and the psychological aspect of addiction.

Ms Sidra Waheed, final-year student of AKU Medical College, presented a surprising "Message for Health Professionals", many of whom are regular smokers in spite of being professionally aware of the consequences. She further articulated the common myth amongst students that smoking relieves stress. The final speaker, Ms Humaira Waheed, from the Department of Nursing Services, AKUH, said that tobacco was a first step to other addictions and portrayed cases from her clinical experiences.
